17-13-0303-C(1) Type 1 Narrative & Plans — 2315 West Grand Avenue, Chicago, IL

Proposed Zoning: B2-5 Neighborhood Mixed-Use District
Lot Area: Approximately 10,080 sq. ft.

Proposed Land Use: The Applicant is proposing to redevelop the subject property with a new
five-story mixed-use building containing 1,613 sq. ft. of commercial/retail
space and an attached off-street parking garage on the first floor. The
proposed building will contain sixteen (16) dwelling units above and will
feature four (4) roof top decks. The proposed building will measure
approximately 57 ft.-2 in. in height. The subject property is a Transit Served
Location and will be supported sixteen (16) off-street parking spaces within
the attached garage. The subject lot is a through lot with two (2) street
frontages (West Grand Avenue to the north and West Ferdinand Street to
the south). Pursuant to Sec. 17-13-0303-D optional Administrative
Adjustment and Variation and pursuant to Secs. 17-13-1003-EE, 17-13-
1003-P, Q, R, and X, and 17-13-1101-B of the Chicago Zoning Ordinance,
the Applicant is seeking to increase the off-street parking ratio from 50% (8
parking spaces) to 100% (16 parking spaces), to not comply with the TSL
design guidelines on the lot’s West Ferdinand Street frontage, to reduce the
ground floor commercial space floor area to 1,613 sq. ft., reduce the front
setback on the subject jot’s West Ferdinand Street frontage for floors
containing residential units from 30 feet to | ft.-6 in., and is seeking all
zoning relief necessary, as needed and as allowed by the Chicago Zoning
Code, for the attached plans.

Sec. 17-3-0308 Criteria for Transit-Served Locations ~ Supplemental Narrative Zoning Analysis

1. The subject property is a designated Transit Served Location per Sec. 17-10-0102-B
because it is located within approximately 400 linear feet of the Western Avenue CTA bus
line corridor. The proposed mixed-use building containing one (1) commercial space and
attached parking garage at grade and sixteen (16) residential units above will be supported
by sixteen (16) off-street parking spaces. Pursuant to Section 17-13-1003-EE, the
Applicant is seeking to permit an increase in the off-street parking ratio from 50% (8
parking spaces) to 100% (16 parking spaces).

2. The Applicant is seeking relief from the requirements of Sec. 17-4-0504 for the location of
the mixed-use building on the subject lot. The subject lot is a through lot with frontage on
both West Grand Avenue and West Ferdinand Street. The proposed location of the main
building door and entryway will be on the lot’s West Grand Avenue frontage and will have
a front setback of zero. The building’s first floor was designed with windows facing the
sidewalk located along West Grand Avenue. The proposed building will have a front
setback of 1 ft.-6 in. from the lot’s West Ferdinand Street frontage.

3. The Transit Friendly Development Guide defines ‘transit friendly development’ as
development which is oriented towards and integrated with adjacent transit. The proposed
mixed-use building incorporates accessibility and connectivity to mass transit based on its
location near the Western Avenue bus line corridor. The Applicant believes the
redevelopment of an underutilized lot will improve the subject area for residents and other
commuters traveling in the subject area.

4. The proposed mixed-use building will contain approximately 1,613 sq. ft. of commercial
space and an attached parking garage on the first floor and sixteen (16) residential units
above. The proposed building will be supported by sixteen (16) off-street parking spaces.
The Applicant is seeking administrative approval to permit the off-street parking increase
for the residential units pursuant to the TOD Ordinance.

5. The Applicant believes the proposed mixed-use building will provide appropriate density
in the subject neighborhood. More specifically, the project will replace an underutilized
lot with a new mixed-use building, which will provide additional residential housing
thereby meeting market demand. Based on the subject property’s proximity to a designated
CTA bus line corridor (Bus Routes 49 and 49x), the Applicant believes the project provides
transit options and otherwise complies with the Travel Demand Study and Management
Plan rules promulgated by the Department of Transportation by serving an area in need.
